name: IL-15
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+20 partisan lean strongly favors Republicans
Incumbent Mary Miller has a large fundraising advantage ($810K to $31K cash)
Prediction markets price Miller at ~96% to win
No public polling of the race
model.rationale: The R+20 district lean, Miller's incumbency and overwhelming financial edge, and markets pricing her near 96% all point to a safe Republican hold; the modest Democratic-leaning national environment is far too small to close an 18-point gap.
model.watch: A major national Democratic wave or unexpected scandal could pull the margin closer, but the seat is very unlikely to flip.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
This heavily Republican southern Illinois district sits about twenty points to the right of the nation, making it difficult terrain for any Democrat. Incumbent Mary Miller is running for another term and holds a decisive financial advantage, with roughly $810,000 on hand compared to about $31,000 for Democrat Jennifer Todd, who has raised little more than $113,000. Outside spending in the race has been minimal so far.

Prediction markets give Miller roughly a 96 percent chance of winning, and no expert raters have flagged the contest as competitive. The Democratic ticket's favorable national environment could shave a few points off the Republican margin, but not nearly enough to threaten the seat. The forecast calls for Miller to win comfortably, with the district's fundamentals doing most of the work.
